parts:
Hi Manisha,

Please keep relevant replies on-list.  That way everyone gets the benefit of the dialogue.

On to your question.  You ask whether ces2 needs to be the same dataset as ces1.  It doesn't - if ces2 was identical to ces1, all you would be doing is using the robust average of the dataset itself as a common reference (and it doesn't make any sense to pool the tumor and normals).  In Henrik's example on the other thread, ces2 is the reference set (normals) - because the reference set is a different size to the data (tumor), ces1, you have to take the robust average of ces2, using getAverageFile(), to get a common reference.

Cheers,

Ken

On Fri, May 30, 2008 at 5:15 AM, Manisha Brahmachary <mb3...@c2b2.columbia.edu> wrote:

Hi Ken,

 

Thanks for answering my queries in the last few days on aroma affymetrix.

 

I am writing this email directly to you to just clarify a point based on a thread in the discussion forum.

 

I have 88 normal samples and 145 tumor samples, unpaired data (Affymetrix SNP_6 array). I want to use the normal samples as my reference set. From the discussion forum on aroma affymetrix I came upon the following thread which kind of answers my question below. However, I wanted to clarify a point before I proceeded to process my samples.

 

The thread:

 

Are you asking how you can use the robust average of the 'ces2' set as the reference to each of the arrays in 'ces1'?  If so, then you have to create a reference set with the same number of arrays and the proceed as in paired analysis:

 

# Create reference set (with identical files) of the same size as 'ces1'.

ceRef <- getAverageFile(ces2);

ceRef$combineAlleles <- ces2$combineAlleles;

ceRef$mergeStrands <- ces2$mergeStrands;

cesRef <- clone(ces2);

cesRef$files <- rep(list(ceRef), nbrOfArrays(ces1));

 

 

# "Paired" analysis

glad <- GladModel(ces1, cesRef)

 

 

I needed to clarify a point in your reply thread above.

 

When I create the reference set ces2, is that suppose to be with the same dataset and same number of files, I use to create ces1?

 

Should ces1 contain both tumor and normal samples?

 

Thanks

Manisha
